1. Set the slide background to light gray #f5f5f5 on a blank layout.

6. At the top inside the cream rectangle, add the dual Lagrangian equation in blue (#0000ff) math font: \mathscr{L}_D(\alpha) = \sum_{i=1}^N \alpha_i - \frac{1}{2} \sum_{j=1}^N \sum_{i=1}^N \alpha_i \alpha_j y_i y_j X_i^T X_j.
7. Below the Lagrangian, add two side-by-side rectangles with white (#ffffff) fill and blue (#0000ff) math text: LEFT box 'W = \sum_{i=1}^N \alpha_i y_i X_i'; RIGHT box 'b = -\frac{1}{2} [\max_{i:y_i=-1} W^T X_i + \min_{i:y_i=+1} W^T X_i]'.
8. Still inside the cream rectangle, centered below the two formula boxes, add an orange/salmon rectangle (#ffcc99 fill) containing the text 'Class of vector Z => sign(W^T Z + b)' in dark red #c00000.

12. Remember row 2: the math line 'X_i^T X_j => φ(X_i)^T φ(X_j)' in blue (#0000ff) math font, with the arrow '=>' in red (#ff0000).
13. Remember row 3: bold red (#ff0000) label 'Kernelization', then 'Instead of using φ(X_i)^T φ(X_j) use K(X_i^T, X_j)' with the math expressions in blue (#0000ff), the connecting words in black (#000000), and the parenthetical '(Where K is one of kernel functions)' in red (#ff0000) italic.
14. In the empty lower-left area below the Remember frame, place one small black mouse-cursor (arrow) icon.
15. Leave the rest of the bottom area empty; the only bottom-edge elements are the cursor icon (step 14) and the black strip (step 2).
